subject.title: [BUG] exec tool: aborted run wedges subsequent exec calls in same session (regression from PR #94412)

question: Should maintainers first require one instrumented current-main reproduction that distinguishes exec completion wake failure from abort-result or session-lane release failure before choosing a repair owner?
rationale: The supplied reports show real user impact but disagree on trigger and active-work kind, so source-level routing cannot safely select a single fix boundary from the issue text alone.

options.title: Capture one owner-level trace
options.body: Record a redacted current-main scenario with exec/process state, terminal outcome, and lane-release events, then assign the verified missing transition.

options.title: Fold into abort-result repair
options.body: Treat this as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/105681 only if its proposed AbortError fix reproduces and removes the session wedge in the reported scenario.

recommendation.title: Capture one owner-level trace
recommendation.body: Record a redacted current-main scenario with exec/process state, terminal outcome, and lane-release events, then assign the verified missing transition.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and refined the shared agent-loop abort boundary implicated by the issue, making them the strongest available routing candidate.
